Curacao Oil & Gas Facilities Seized in Ongoing Geopolitical Standoff

WILLEMSTAD, June 14—Curacao’s oil and gas sector was thrown into turmoil on Friday after authorities seized several major industry sites on the island, targeting assets linked to foreign-owned producers in response to an escalating geopolitical dispute. The move, which began early Thursday, has disrupted operations at multiple terminals and refineries, with BB Energy Holdings NV among the firms affected.

Officials in Willemstad said the seizures were necessary to “safeguard national interests” amid what they described as “external pressures” related to ongoing international tensions. “This action is not taken lightly, but we must ensure Curacao’s resources are protected,” said Energy Minister Lucia Martens at a press conference. She declined to specify the expected duration of the measure.

The blockade of key facilities, including the Isla terminal and at least two offshore loading points, has already halted crude transshipments and forced the suspension of refining activities. Workers arriving Friday morning were turned away by security forces. “We are deeply concerned for our members’ jobs and safety,” said Juan Rosario, president of the Petroleum Workers Union. “The situation is tense, and we are seeking urgent clarification from the government.”

BB Energy Holdings NV, which manages storage and shipment operations at one of the affected sites, confirmed disruptions in a brief statement. “Our operations in Curacao are currently suspended due to circumstances beyond our control,” the company said, adding it was “monitoring the situation closely and cooperating with local authorities.”

Industry analysts estimate that over 150,000 barrels per day of throughput have been impacted, with potential knock-on effects for regional supply chains. “Curacao is a strategic logistics hub for oil and gas producers serving both the Caribbean and trans-Atlantic routes,” noted Rafael Fernandez, a consultant with Caribbean Energy Insight. “Any prolonged disruption here could ripple across global markets.”

There was no immediate indication when the standoff might be resolved. The Petroleum Producers Association of Curacao urged “all parties to pursue dialogue” to prevent lasting damage to the sector. The government said further updates would be provided “as the situation develops.”
